title: THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN
author: CLAUDE

rounds.summary: This is the slate's cleanest ordinary-human test of R11. Iveth's concrete aim is to save the village through inherited slow-fire knowledge; Brandt's is to keep three hundred people alive while obeying a lawful evacuation order shaped by his own record of loss. Illuminara must first understand the stone-wall and terrace pattern, then turn empathy into action by giving both Iveth's knowledge and Brandt's responsibility a place in a single command. The result is physical and measurable rather than rhetorical: a jointly completed break that holds when the wind turns, with loss and accountability still visible.
Built the complete first draft of THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN, with explicit goals, a falsifiable test, freely chosen cooperation and a material positive result that preserves remaining costs.

A vivid, unusually disciplined first draft makes inherited fire knowledge, public command and scientific modelling genuinely interdependent. Ivet's practice is neither mysticism nor a universal cure; Brandt's Calder Fold memory gives his refusal moral and operational weight; Illuminara listens, finds the north-gully exception and offers a test that Brandt may stop. The dialogue has distinct pressure and dry wit, the two cottages remain a real cost, and the final report preserves both responsibility and knowledge. Before final, the safety logic needs one coherent abort rule, the thirty-metre test must not be allowed to prove more than it measures, and Ivet should freely own the corrected limit of her map so that the final alliance is earned by all three rather than conferred on her after success.

ACCEPTED: The abort number did three jobs in one sentence. It is now split by phase and each phase has one action: before ignition thirty-five cancels the burn; after the strip is cold a gust past thirty-five or an ember across a wall means no further lighting and every crew behind the car park wall, strip left to work; Brandt never chases a headfire. The wind-turn scene carries it through: gauge 29, 33, 34, then 36, and Brandt executes the withdrawal on the radio. At ten past five, before ignition, the gauge reads eighteen and he says Light, so the first phase is also seen. Nobody goes up the Marrick track, and the reason (it is the wrong side of the line) is stated at the cottages. No promise to extinguish the uncontrolled headfire remains. ACCEPTED: The pre-fire plan now fixes the geometry before the sluice opens: 240 metres from sluice to Marrick fence, three terraces, the third at 180 metres, eleven minutes per hundred metres, sluice at ten to five, wet front past the third terrace at ten past, with one failure signal (no wet front there by ten past five means no torch and crews to the car park wall). The wet and black bands end at the fence; the two cottages sit forty metres beyond any water she can carry, said before the fire. Illuminara says the wall test proves one wall and sets the gully prediction (slows to a crawl on the wet band) against the rival failure signal (flame standing on a bank); the headfire scene reports her reading, Slowing and Banks clear. Also repaired a timeline fault in my draft, where the margins would have been lit at twenty to six, at the moment of the wind turn; they are now lit at ten past five and finished before the turn. T03 resolves all three T02 priorities without sacrificing the draft's distinctive voices, bounded costs or three-way agency. Brandt's thirty-five threshold now has phase-specific actions and is executed at thirty-six; the gully plan freezes its distance, clock, protected boundary and failure signal before ignition, while the one-wall test remains only one-wall evidence; and Ivet freely accepts a supervised, stoppable practice while Brandt reciprocates with a trial and hearing support rather than pardon or automatic adoption. The result is operationally legible, emotionally earned and fully aligned with R11 section 17. No further developmental revision is required before the author seals this exact story as AUTHOR_FINAL.
Sealed the exact source-bound final of THE FIRE THAT KNEW HOW TO BURN after the reviewed author line was complete; any same-text predecessor is preserved in the version series.

An old woman's forbidden firecraft, a chief's fatal memory and Illuminara's water model become a bounded, stoppable defence that saves Sorrel Gate because each of them is willing to find where their own map is wrong.
